text: {"score":3,"justification":"Numbers match the card and the tool outputs, the language is cautious, and the next step of requesting targeted 99215 charts is concrete. But the headline contradicts the body, the text has several inconsistencies, and the investigator still has to redo analysis.","problems":["Headline says \"charts support the billing\", but the body calls the case inconclusive and says the charts \"do not settle it\". This is an overclaim built on only 7 documented 99215 claims.","The headline says the share is \"elevated in every complexity group\", but the card shows the 0-condition group at 12.5% against 1.8% overall. That is elevated, but the claim is not explained, and the heavy rise in high-complexity groups (80-86%) is not discussed.","The rationale never uses the strongest evidence: 99215 share by complexity, with 0-1 condition patients at 12-17% against 1.8-3% for all providers. It also does not mention the excess of about 92 claims, or that 85% of 99215 claims were on patients with 2 or more conditions.","It states \"the panel is moderately complex\" with no supporting number. It also says \"the claims are unresolved\", which is vague.","Duplicate-note rate 21% appears without interpretation. It does not match the hybrid_review figure visible in the tool output. It is not flagged as a concern and is not linked to a next step.","Two of the three cited examples are low-complexity 99215 claims. The third, C0078030, is a 99213 below-billed example, so it fits the below-billed point but not a 99215 sample request. The summary also ignores 99215 claims that were documented as supported, such as C0078017.","The 'no audit trail received' and deficiency notes (MISSING_SIGNATURE, MISSING_RESULTS) are not turned into specific follow-up requests. The next steps do not ask for audit trails or lab results.","The summary says 29 records came back, but does not point out that the sample was random rather than targeted at 99215, which is why only 7 documented 99215 claims exist."]}
